records.title: How should passwords be protected?
records.content: Applications should not store passwords in plain text. Passwords should be processed with a suitable password-hashing algorithm and appropriate parameters, such as Argon2id or an appropriately configured bcrypt implementation. Password verification should use the corresponding password-hashing library. Review the actual backend implementation before claiming that HisabDo follows these practices.

records.title: How should authentication tokens be protected?
records.content: Authentication tokens should be protected from disclosure and unauthorized use. Use HTTPS in deployed environments, keep signing secrets out of source control, validate token signatures and relevant claims on the server, and apply suitable expiration and revocation strategies. Development-only token endpoints should not be exposed in production. Confirm the application's token validation, secret management, and endpoint configuration before claiming these controls are implemented.

records.title: What should I do about suspicious financial activity?
records.content: If you notice suspicious activity, contact the relevant financial institution or official service support promptly. If banking or payment credentials may be compromised, contact the institution using a trusted official channel and follow its instructions to secure the account. Change compromised passwords from a trusted device and review recent account activity. Do not share authentication codes or passwords with anyone claiming to provide support.

records.title: How can an application reduce unauthorized login attempts?
records.content: Authentication endpoints should use appropriately configured rate limiting and abuse protections. Applications should validate credentials on the server, avoid revealing whether a username or password was incorrect in a way that enables account enumeration, and monitor suspicious login activity. The exact controls and thresholds must be selected for the application's risk and architecture. Verify the deployed backend before claiming these protections are active.
